items.quote: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was carried out in a JEOL Superprobe 733.
XRD was carried out in a DRON-3 diffractometer on metallographic sections for ductile samples and on powders for brittle samples, respectively.

items.instrument: Gemini 1550 scanning electron microscope equipped with an INCA analysis system
items.quote: The integral chemical composition of the samples was measured by EDS in a Gemini 1550 scanning electron microscope equipped with an INCA analysis system.
The solidus temperature for the samples nos. 2, 3, 7 and 11 (incipient melting) were also determined using the method devised by Pirani and Alterthum [31].
Its maximum instrumental errors amount to ±2.8 K for the temperature region 1200-1700 K and ±4 K for 1700-2300 K.
items.stated_uncertainty: ±2.8 K for the temperature region 1200-1700 K and ±4 K for 1700-2300 K

items.quote: The DTA measurements were performed under high purity He with heating and cooling rates of 20 or 40 K min-1 .

items.calibration: W/W-20Re string thermocouples designed by Kocherzhinsky et al. [29,30]
items.quote: Temperatures of solid-state and solid-liquid phase transformations were determined by DTA using Sc2 O3 crucibles and W/W-20Re string thermocouples designed by Kocherzhinsky et al. [29,30].

The method is well described in Refs. [33,34] and involves the determination of the enthalpy of dissolution of pure solid Al, Nb, Ti as well as that of the alloy in liquid Ni at 1773 ± 5 K by drop isoperibolic calorimetry.

items.label: 26 different samples
items.quote: In order to verify phase equilibria in the Al-Nb and Al-Nb-Ti systems a number of 26 different samples, with a mass of 15 or 20 g each, were prepared (Table 2) by arc melting with a non-consumable tungsten electrode on a water-cooled copper hearth under purified Ar (cooling rates of about 100 K s-1 ).
items.synthesis: arc melting with a non-consumable tungsten electrode on a water-cooled copper hearth under purified Ar (cooling rates of about 100 K s-1 )

items.label: samples nos. 2, 3, 7 and 11
items.quote: The solidus temperature for the samples nos. 2, 3, 7 and 11 (incipient melting) were also determined using the method devised by Pirani and Alterthum [31].

items.label: no. 18 in Table 2
items.quote: Within the frame of the present work the standard enthalpy of formation at 298 K was experimentally determined for the ␥ single-phase sample Ti25.3 Nb19.0 Al55.7 (no. 18 in Table 2) annealed for 8 h at 1673 K.

items.nominal_composition: nominal Nb content of 8 at.% and Al contents of 45, 46, 47 and 48 at.%, respectively
items.quote: Fig. 6 depicts selected heating curves obtained by DTA for a series of samples with the nominal Nb content of 8 at.% and Al contents of 45, 46, 47 and 48 at.%, respectively.

Within the frame of the present work the standard enthalpy of formation at 298 K was experimentally determined for the ␥ single-phase sample Ti25.3 Nb19.0 Al55.7 (no. 18 in Table 2) annealed for 8 h at 1673 K.
